description: Apply the SE-EDU intermediate Java coding standard when writing, reviewing, or refactoring Java in this project.
to every production and test Java change in this repository. Preserve existing
behavior unless the user requests a behavioral change.
- Use lowercase package names; PascalCase nouns for types; camelCase verbs for
methods; and camelCase variables. Use `is`, `has`, `can`, or similar prefixes
for booleans and plural names for collections. Test methods may use
- Use four spaces for indentation, K&R braces, braces for every loop and
conditional body, and a maximum line length of 120 characters (prefer 110).
Wrap for readability, with continuation indentation eight spaces beyond the
parent line; break after commas and before operators.
- Keep imports explicit and consistently grouped: Java imports first, followed
by a blank line and project or third-party imports. Do not use wildcard
- Declare variables in the smallest useful scope and initialize them at
declaration when a valid initial value is available. Do not expose mutable
- Write comments in English using American spelling. Give every public class
and public method a JavaDoc header unless it is a getter, setter, an exact
override, or test code. Begin the summary with a verb such as “Returns” or
“Adds”, use complete sentences, and end `@param`, `@return`, and `@throws`
Before handing off Java changes, check that the changed files meet these rules
and run the project verification required by `AGENTS.md`.

description: Run and verify planned terminal UI tests for this Java project. Use when asked to test Bambolino's console interface, run UI regression tests, compare commands with expected output, or show a console test-session record.
Run the test plan at `test/ui-test-plan.md` with:
Each test case must use this exact structure. `Expected output` starts after Bambolino's startup greeting; the full startup greeting is still included in the generated transcript.
Bye. Hope to see you again soon!

Add tests in the order they should run. The runner compiles all files in `src/main/java` using Java 25, runs each test in a fresh application process, and compares its output exactly. It ends immediately at the first failing test and reports both expected and actual output.
After every run, inspect `test/ui-test-session.md` for the console input and output of every test that ran. Do not edit that generated record manually.

This repository is a starter template for a greenfield Java project used in an introductory software engineering course in an undergraduate computer science program. Students use it as the starting point for their own projects.

Unless the user says otherwise, assume that you are assisting a student working on a project in this repository. If the user identifies themselves as an instructor or another project stakeholder, adapt your response to that role.
* Prior knowledge: Basic Java and OOP concepts.
* Level of programming experience: Beginner to intermediate.
* IDE and level of expertise: Beginner in using IntelliJ IDEA.
* Explain the rationale for significant actions: what you did and why.
* Keep explanations brief but instructive, supporting learning through responsible use of AI. For example:
* When suggesting a Git command, briefly explain what it does.
* Add explanatory Javadoc comments to all classes and to nontrivial methods and fields when their purpose or behavior is not obvious.
* Make generated code as self-explanatory as possible, and include explanatory comments where they improve understanding.
* When faced with a design choice, choose the simplest option that is sufficient for the requirements, while briefly explaining relevant more advanced alternatives.
Ensure that Java 25 is used when running the application or build tasks. On macOS, use `sdk use java 25.0.3.fx-zulu` to switch to Java 25 if needed.
Before writing, reviewing, or modifying Java code, use the project-specific `$seedu-java-coding-standard` skill and comply with its rules.

After every code update, review `test/ui-test-plan.md` and update its test cases when the changed behaviour needs new or revised coverage. Then invoke the project-specific `$test-ui` skill by running:
Stop and report the failure if the UI test run does not pass. The runner records the console input and output in `test/ui-test-session.md`.
Before proposing or creating a commit, use the project-specific `$seedu-git-standard` skill and comply with its rules.
Use lightweight tags unless the user requests an annotated tag.
When proposing or creating a commit message, include enough detail to explain the rationale for the change.
Do not commit or push unless explicitly asked.
